findings.text: §28 blames the previous attempt's stream for the stale quiet time, but the code at the reviewed revision already measures quiet as `min(now - newest_stream_write, now - attempt_clock)` (`_run_stream_quiet_seconds`, reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:567-601) — the cap is 8 days old — and `_attempt_started_seconds` (recovery_liveness.py:402-421) reads `attempt_started_at` off the pointer first and falls back to `attempt.json` only when the pointer omits the field, so a resume window in which the pointer still names the previous attempt yields `min(17m, 17m) = 17m` and a `stalled` row reading "liveness unknown, quiet 17m" — exactly the measured row — with no stream-only reading anywhere on that path; a node that implements the deliverable's wording as "cap the stream's quiet at `attempt.json`'s start" without also changing the pointer-first precedence leaves the incident reproducing
